description: An experiment variant spec is valid when a control group is declared, every variant has a feature flag and terminal outcomes, analytics events are consistent across all variants, no variant bypasses security constraints, and rollback behavior is explicitly defined.

rules.description: experiment-variant-spec.json must exist with experiment_id, hypothesis, and variants array of at least 2. Experiments without a spec cannot be validated.
Every variant must declare id, name, flowRef, and featureFlag. Variants without these fields cannot be activated or identified in analytics.
Exactly one variant must have isControl:true. Without a control group, there is no baseline to compare experiment results against.
Every variant's featureFlag must be a non-empty string. Variants without a feature flag cannot be activated programmatically and cannot be part of the experiment.

Every variant must declare a terminals array with at least one terminal of type success, failure, or abandoned, each with a description. Variants without terminal outcomes cannot be statistically analyzed.
If analyticsEvents is declared at the spec level, every variant must track the same event names. Variants that miss events create gaps in experiment data that invalidate statistical analysis.
No variant may declare bypassAuth:true, bypassValidation:true, or skipGuards:true. Experiments are never an excuse to disable security constraints regardless of the hypothesis being tested.
Spec must declare rollbackBehavior as revert-to-control, disable-experiment, or gradual-ramp-down. Experiments without a rollback plan cannot be stopped safely when they need to be terminated.
All variant ids must be unique within the spec. Duplicate variant ids cause conflicting feature flag resolution and broken analytics attribution.
Both experiment_id and hypothesis must be non-empty strings. Experiments without a unique id cannot be tracked, and experiments without a hypothesis are undirected guesses.
